body:
Atomic energy and its applications

Atomic energy is energy associated with changes in atomic nuclei. In nuclear power stations, controlled nuclear fission releases heat, which can be used to produce electricity. Radioactive materials also have applications in medicine, agriculture, industry and scientific research.

The institutions responsible for research, power generation and radiation safety perform different functions. Understanding these distinctions is essential for identifying their mandates correctly.

Department of Atomic Energy

The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) was established on 3 August 1954 under the direct charge of the Prime Minister. It is responsible for major aspects of India's atomic-energy programme, including research and development and peaceful applications of nuclear science.

The Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) is responsible for formulating DAE policy. The present institutional structure includes the Commission constituted by government resolution on 1 March 1958.

Bhabha Atomic Research Centre

The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is a major nuclear research institution at Trombay, Mumbai. It developed from the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET), established in January 1954 under Homi J. Bhabha's leadership. Following his death, AEET was renamed BARC in 1967.

BARC conducts research and development in nuclear science and associated technologies. Its work includes nuclear materials, research reactors, radiation-related applications and other scientific fields relevant to the atomic-energy programme.

A research reactor is used principally for research, testing, training or producing useful isotopes. It should not automatically be described as a commercial electricity-generating power station.

Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited

The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) is a public-sector enterprise under DAE. It was registered in September 1987 and is responsible for activities involving the design, construction, commissioning and operation of nuclear power reactors for electricity generation.

Kakrapar Atomic Power Station (KAPS), located in the Tapi district of Gujarat, is an important regional example of nuclear electricity generation. It is operated within the NPCIL system.

Atomic Energy Regulatory Board

The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) was constituted on 15 November 1983 under powers provided by the Atomic Energy Act, 1962. Its main responsibility is nuclear and radiological safety.

AERB regulates activities involving nuclear energy and ionising radiation to protect people and the environment from undue risk. Its safety responsibilities extend beyond power stations to relevant radiation applications in medicine, industry and research.

NPCIL operates nuclear power reactors; AERB performs safety-regulatory functions. The two should not be confused. AERB's role is regulation, not commercial generation of electricity.

Institute for Plasma Research: Gujarat connection

The Institute for Plasma Research (IPR) is situated near Gandhinagar, Gujarat. It was established in 1986 under DST and came under the DAE administrative framework in 1995. It is an aided research institute working on plasma science and associated technologies, including research relevant to fusion.

Plasma is a state of matter containing charged particles. Nuclear fusion involves combining light nuclei, while nuclear fission involves splitting heavy nuclei. Research on fusion should not be confused with the fission-based electricity production at existing conventional nuclear power stations.

Prelims focus

  • DAE: established 3 August 1954.
  • BARC: Trombay, Mumbai; AEET was renamed BARC in 1967.
  • NPCIL: formed in 1987; nuclear power generation.
  • AERB: constituted 15 November 1983; nuclear and radiation safety.
  • Kakrapar Atomic Power Station: Tapi district, Gujarat.
  • IPR: Gandhinagar; plasma research; under DAE administration since 1995.
  • Trap: Plasma and fusion research at IPR is not the same function as operating nuclear power reactors at NPCIL.

[Department of Atomic Energy, History, establishment of DAE and Atomic Energy Commission; Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, About Us; Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, About NPCIL and Kakrapar Gujarat Site information; Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, About Us and Constitution Order dated 15 November 1983; Institute for Plasma Research, Campuses and About Us; sources consulted 2 November 2026.]

title: Atomic Energy Institutions: DAE, BARC, NPCIL, AERB and IPR

body:
Medical research and public health

Medical research investigates human health, disease, diagnosis, prevention and treatment. It also examines how health problems affect populations. These findings can guide clinical practice, public-health programmes and the development of medical products.

Research and healthcare delivery are related but different. A research institution investigates evidence and develops knowledge; hospitals and health services provide care to patients. Some institutions perform both functions, but their principal mandates should be identified accurately.

Indian Council of Medical Research

The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) is India's apex organisation for the formulation, coordination and promotion of biomedical research. It functions within the Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

Its predecessor, the Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA), was established in 1911. It was subsequently renamed the Indian Council of Medical Research in 1949.

ICMR coordinates and conducts research related to important health problems. Its work includes infectious diseases, nutrition, non-communicable diseases, occupational health and other public-health concerns. It also supports the translation of medical research into useful approaches for prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

Important ICMR institutes

InstitutionLocationMain research area
ICMR-National Institute of VirologyPuneViruses and viral diseases.
ICMR-National Institute of NutritionHyderabadNutrition and related health research.
ICMR-National Institute of Occupational Health ResearchAhmedabadOccupational and environmental health.

Occupational health concerns the protection of people from health risks associated with their work. The Ahmedabad institute is an especially relevant Gujarat example. Its current name is ICMR-National Institute of Occupational Health Research (ICMR-NIOHR).

Department of Biotechnology

The Department of Biotechnology (DBT) was established in 1986 under the Union Ministry of Science and Technology. It promotes biotechnology research, education, technological development and applications across sectors.

Biotechnology uses living organisms, cells or biological processes to develop useful products and services. Examples include improved crops, diagnostic methods, biological medicines and industrial processes involving microorganisms.

DBT and ICMR have overlapping interests in health-related biotechnology, but their mandates differ. ICMR is primarily concerned with biomedical and health research. DBT supports biotechnology across health, agriculture, industry and other fields.

For example, research into a disease may involve ICMR-supported biomedical studies, while research into a biotechnology-based diagnostic product may also receive support from DBT programmes. Participation in a related field does not make the two organisations identical.

Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre

The Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC) is an autonomous organisation of the Government of Gujarat's Department of Science and Technology. It was created by a government resolution dated 11 August 2017 and commenced functioning on 1 September 2017.

GBRC is based in Gandhinagar. It supports biotechnology research relevant to healthcare, agriculture, industry, the environment and marine resources. It also provides shared research facilities and supports collaboration with academic institutions and other organisations.

From medical evidence to public benefit

When a health problem is identified, researchers may investigate its causes, distribution and possible interventions. Scientific findings can then inform diagnostic methods, prevention strategies or medical guidelines. The value of this work depends on reliable evidence and appropriate implementation.

The distinction between health research and healthcare administration is important. ICMR is an important source of biomedical research, but it should not be confused with every hospital, drug regulator or public-health service provider.

Prelims focus

  • ICMR: apex body for biomedical research.
  • IRFA: established in 1911; renamed ICMR in 1949.
  • ICMR-National Institute of Virology: Pune.
  • ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition: Hyderabad.
  • ICMR-NIOHR: Ahmedabad; occupational and environmental health.
  • DBT: established in 1986; biotechnology across multiple sectors.
  • GBRC: Gandhinagar; established under a 2017 Gujarat government resolution.
  • Trap: DBT is not limited to medical research, and ICMR is not a general biotechnology department.

[Indian Council of Medical Research, History, entries for 1911 and 1949; ICMR, Vision, Mission and Mandate; ICMR, Institutes, entries for National Institute of Virology, National Institute of Nutrition and National Institute of Occupational Health Research; Department of Biotechnology, historical overview of the department's establishment in 1986; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre, Overview and Formation; NCERT, Biology, Class 12, Chapter 12: Biotechnology and Its Applications, opening section; sources consulted 2 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: National ICMR focuses on health research, DBT spans biotechnology sectors, and Gujarat's GBRC works at state level; diagnostics can overlap.
pictures.caption: Medical research and biotechnology overlap, but their institutions have different scopes.

title: Medical Research and Biotechnology Institutions: ICMR, DBT and Gujarat Centres

body:
Why is agricultural research important?

Agriculture depends on soil, water, climate, plants, animals and human management. Scientific research can help improve crop varieties, protect plants from diseases, conserve resources and increase the quality of agricultural production.

However, the usefulness of a technology must be evaluated under the conditions in which farmers will apply it. A crop variety that performs well in one environment may not be equally suitable everywhere. This makes field evaluation and communication between researchers and farmers essential.

Indian Council of Agricultural Research

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is India's apex organisation for coordinating, guiding and managing research and education in agriculture and allied sectors.

ICAR was established on 16 July 1929 as the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research. It is now an autonomous organisation under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Its headquarters is in New Delhi.

ICAR's work covers crop science, horticulture, animal sciences, fisheries, natural-resource management and agricultural education. Agricultural research is therefore broader than the development of cereal crops alone.

Research, education and extension

The agricultural knowledge system performs three connected functions:

  • Research: Developing and assessing improved scientific knowledge and technologies.
  • Education: Training students and professionals in agricultural sciences.
  • Extension: Helping farmers and rural communities understand and use relevant scientific knowledge.

Agricultural extension is the process of communicating research findings and practical guidance to farmers. It can include training, field demonstrations, advisory services and feedback about problems encountered in actual farming conditions.

Krishi Vigyan Kendras

Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are important frontline agricultural extension institutions operating at the district level. They connect scientific research with farmers' needs through local assessment, demonstrations and training.

The first KVK was established in Puducherry in 1974. KVKs support activities such as demonstrations of agricultural technologies, training for farmers and rural youth, farm advisories and the communication of locally relevant practices.

For example, an agricultural research institute may identify a suitable method for reducing unnecessary irrigation. A KVK may assess the method under local farm conditions and demonstrate its use to farmers. Farmers' experiences can also provide valuable feedback for further research.

Important ICAR institutions in Gujarat

ICAR-Indian Institute of Groundnut Research (ICAR-IIGR), Junagadh focuses on research related to groundnut. Groundnut is an important agricultural crop in Gujarat, making the location and specialisation useful for regional examination preparation.

ICAR-Directorate of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants Research (ICAR-DMAPR), Anand is associated with research on medicinal and aromatic plants.

These are specialised institutions within the national agricultural research system. Their work differs from the district-level extension function of a KVK.

Connecting agricultural science with other disciplines

Agricultural research uses knowledge from biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science and biotechnology. Plant breeding, for example, aims to develop crops with desirable properties such as improved yield, quality or resistance to disease.

Scientific improvements must also be considered alongside soil health, water availability and environmental effects. Producing more food without damaging natural resources is a major reason for combining agricultural research with sustainable farm management.

Prelims focus

  • ICAR was established on 16 July 1929.
  • Its original name was Imperial Council of Agricultural Research.
  • ICAR functions under DARE, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
  • First KVK: Puducherry, 1974.
  • ICAR-IIGR: Junagadh; groundnut research.
  • ICAR-DMAPR: Anand; medicinal and aromatic plants.
  • Trap: ICAR coordinates agricultural research and education, while KVKs primarily connect research with farmers through frontline extension.
